deliverables.title: F-0.2.17-W4-001 closure: ChromaDB re-index hook in gap_carry_forward_writer.append_to_file + unit tests + live verification

additions: OTEL counter `aho.gap_carry_forward_writer.reindex_failures` (created at module import, no-op when opentelemetry absent)
regex CARRY_FWD_FILENAME_RE matching `carry-forwards-{X.Y.Z}.md` for iteration label extraction

_trigger_reindex(file_path) - extracts iteration from filename (filename takes precedence over AHO_ITERATION env), reads project from AHO_PROJECT env (default 'ahomw'), invokes aho.rag.index_artifact with workstream='carry-forwards'; catches (RagError, RagInputError, OSError, ImportError) and degrades to warning + counter increment without blocking the append
_record_reindex_failure(file_path, iteration, error_type, error_message) - emits stderr warning + OTEL counter add with attrs {file_path, iteration, error_type}
append_to_file return dict gains a 'reindex' field with reindex_status / iteration / project / doc_id (on success) or error (on failure)
code_change.best_effort_contract: append_to_file is the load-bearing primitive - file write happens BEFORE reindex; reindex failure (Ollama down, ChromaDB missing, etc.) does NOT block the append return. The append's structural success is the F-0.2.17-W4-001 closure invariant; reindex is best-effort staleness avoidance.

tests.name: test_append_triggers_reindex_on_success
tests.asserts: fake rag.index_artifact invoked with project=ahomw, iteration=0.2.16 (parsed from filename), workstream='carry-forwards'; reindex_status='ok'; entries_added==1

tests.name: test_append_succeeds_when_reindex_raises
tests.asserts: FakeRagError raised by mock index_artifact; append still returned with entries_added==1; reindex_status='failed'; stderr WARNING emitted

tests.name: test_iteration_label_from_filename_overrides_env
tests.asserts: AHO_ITERATION=9.9.9 env var ignored when filename is carry-forwards-0.2.16.md; reindex called with iteration='0.2.16'

live_verification_probe.method: snapshot pre-sha → append F-0.2.17-W6-PROBE entry via append_to_file (triggers reindex) → query rag for the probe content (best-effort similarity check) → deterministic chunk-scan via collection.get(where=path) verifying any chunk contains the probe ID → restore original file content → re-index restored content → verify post-restore sha matches pre-sha
live_verification_probe.drafter_input_observation_on_query_ranki: embedding-similarity query for the probe-id text did not surface the probe-containing chunk in top 10 results. Top results were 0.2.17 plan-docs / close-notes / W0 amendment archive, ranked higher by recency-weighting + similarity to query-string substrings. The deterministic chunk-scan via chromadb.collection.get(where=path) confirms the chunk IS in the index. F-0.2.17-W4-001 closure scope is staleness elimination on append - that is verified. RAG ranking quality on a generic query string is a separate concern (latent - would surface as a 0.3.x carry-forward IF a query consumer reports false-negatives in practice; not surfaced as a W6 carry-forward).

substrate_observation_during_probe_runs.ollama_state: qwen3.5:9b held ~7.4GB VRAM at probe-run start (loaded by aho-nemoclaw or aho-openclaw user-service); each /api/embed call triggered a nomic-embed-text cold-load (model swap). First embed completed in ~25s; subsequent calls of large carry-forwards file (~50KB → 13 chunks) timed out at default AHO_COUNCIL_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S=30s.
substrate_observation_during_probe_runs.remediation_in_session: Set AHO_COUNCIL_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S=300; live probe then completed reindex_status=ok end-to-end.
substrate_observation_during_probe_runs.drafter_input_observation: the default 30s timeout is too tight for large iteration-scoped artifacts on hardware with co-resident large models. Same shape as 0.2.15 substrate findings (cross-model cascades serialize on 8GB VRAM; Ollama state hygiene is infrastructure). Not a W4-001 regression - the hook itself works; only the tight default timeout surfaces under VRAM contention. Drafter to consider: bump default AHO_COUNCIL_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S in council/embed.py from 30 → 120 (latent - stronger default for production hosts under contention; 0.3.x scope, not W6).

evidence.f_w4_001_closure_invariant: after this commit, any aho.gap_carry_forward_writer.append_to_file call (including write_carry_forward) triggers a ChromaDB re-index of the same file post-write. Audit-time RAG enrichment will see the appended entries on the next audit run that follows an append, removing the staleness mode F-0.2.17-W4-001 captured.

deliverables.notes: Hook implementation lands in src/aho/gap_carry_forward_writer.py. Three unit tests pass - success path, failure-handling path (append still succeeds when reindex raises), and filename-iteration extraction precedence. Live verification probe exercises the full round-trip with byte-perfect file rollback; deterministic chunk-scan confirms the probe-containing chunk is in chromadb after append. Substrate observation about embed timeout under VRAM contention captured for drafter consideration.

data_level_evidence_d2_closure_works_at_.rationale: Even though F-0.2.17-W4-001 surfaces as unverified in the audit, direct chromadb inspection confirms the carry-forwards file IS indexed and the W4-001-containing chunk IS present. The unverified status is from the lookup primitive's ranking, not from staleness/missing-data.
data_level_evidence_d2_closure_works_at_.verification_method: collection.get(where={source_artifact_path: <carry-forwards-path>}) returns 31 chunks; literal substring scan finds 'F-0.2.17-W4-001' in chunk015 (new carry-forwards-workstream chunk) - verified twice independently (during D2 live probe and during this D3 halt-investigation)

lookup_ranking_failure_mode.where_unverified_status_originates: src/aho/council/audit_ref_lookup.py - DEFAULT_K_PER_REF=3 with DEFAULT_POOL_MULTIPLIER=8 means lookup pulls top 24 chunks by cosine similarity for the embedded ID query, then filters to chunks containing the literal ID substring; if no chunk in top-24 contains the literal ID, status=unverified.
lookup_ranking_failure_mode.why_w4_001_misses_top_24: ChromaDB has 158 total chunks; querying with embedded text 'F-0.2.17-W4-001' (an opaque alphanumeric ID) returns top-24 by cosine similarity. The carry-forwards file's chunk015 (which DOES contain the literal F-0.2.17-W4-001 token) does not rank in top-24 against this opaque-ID query because (a) opaque-ID embeddings carry low similarity signal - the embedding doesn't strongly anchor on alphanumeric token shape; (b) the 158-chunk corpus has many other chunks that score higher on cosine similarity for the same embedding query; (c) recency-weighting at AHO_ITERATION=0.2.17 boosts 0.2.17 chunks over 0.2.16 carry-forwards-file chunks.
lookup_ranking_failure_mode.evidence_log: Direct lookup_references invocation against text 'audit refs: F-0.2.17-W1-001 and F-0.2.17-W4-001' returns retrievals=3 for W1-001 (all from W1-close-note.md and W2-plan-doc.md - separate artifacts that mention W1-001), retrievals=0 for W4-001. W1-001 lands registered because W1-close-note.md / W2-plan-doc.md mention it; W4-001 lands unverified because no other artifact mentions W4-001 except the carry-forwards file itself, and the carry-forwards chunk doesn't rank top-24 for the W4-001 opaque-ID query.
lookup_ranking_failure_mode.shape_relationship_to_d2_evidence: Same shape as D2 live probe drafter-input observation: 'embedding-similarity query for the probe-id text did not surface the probe-containing chunk in top 10 results... deterministic chunk-scan confirms the chunk IS in the index.' D3 manifests the same shape on the audit-time RAG enrichment path.
lookup_ranking_failure_mode.implication_for_f_w4_001_closure_claim: AT THE DATA LEVEL: D2 closure works - the hook fires on append, the file is re-indexed, chunks containing the appended IDs are in chromadb (verified twice independently). AT THE LOOKUP LEVEL: the audit_ref_lookup primitive's top-24 ranking by cosine similarity does NOT consistently surface registered carry-forward chunks for opaque-ID queries against the project corpus. Drafter arbitration: is F-0.2.17-W4-001 closed (data-level fix lands) or is the closure incomplete (auditor lookup must consistently see the IDs as registered to count as closed)?
drafter_input_options_for_arbitration: Option A - accept closure as data-level: F-0.2.17-W4-001 is structurally closed (re-index hook lands, chromadb has the data). The audit-time unverified status is a separate lookup-ranking concern; capture it as a new W6-001 carry-forward (lookup-ranking 0.3.x base-tier hardening target). Audit_status transitions pending_drafter_review with W4-001 closure standing and W6-001 added.

Option B - closure incomplete: F-0.2.17-W4-001 closure requires the auditor to see the IDs as registered. Either tighten the lookup primitive (larger pool multiplier, lower similarity threshold) or augment the carry-forwards index with ID-keyed metadata so opaque-ID queries hit consistently. Either path adds W6 D2 follow-up scope; W6 audit_status remains blocked until the follow-up lands.

Option C - partial closure: F-0.2.17-W4-001 closure is structurally landed (data-level) BUT the audit-time staleness signal still fires because of unrelated lookup-ranking concerns. This is captured as F-0.2.17-W6-001 (lookup-ranking, separate from W4-001), and W4-001 itself is closed. Same as Option A but explicit about the partial-closure framing.

carry_forwards_added.title: Audit-time lookup ranking misses opaque-ID matches in carry-forwards file
carry_forwards_added.what_surfaced: audit_ref_lookup retrieves top-24 chunks by cosine similarity then filters to literal-ID-containing chunks. Opaque alphanumeric IDs (F-0.2.17-WN-NNN shape) carry low embedding signal; recency-weighting boosts current-iteration chunks over the 0.2.16 carry-forwards file; 158-chunk corpus has many higher-cosine competitors. The chunk containing the literal token IS in chromadb but does not rank top-24 → status=unverified surfaces in audit RAG enrichment.
carry_forwards_added.mechanism: data IS in chromadb (chunk015 of carry-forwards-workstream chunks for the carry-forwards file path); lookup top-24 doesn't return it. Verified twice independently during W6 D2 live probe and W6 D3 halt-investigation. Empirical test: lookup_references on text 'audit refs: F-0.2.17-W1-001 and F-0.2.17-W4-001' returns retrievals=3 for W1-001 (mentioned in W1-close-note.md + W2-plan-doc.md, separate artifacts), retrievals=0 for W4-001 (mentioned only in carry-forwards file).
carry_forwards_added.disposition: Drafter recommends structural fix (c) - add ID-keyed metadata field at index time so direct lookup by ID-token avoids cosine entirely. Alternative options: (a) larger pool multiplier (statistical, less robust); (b) lower threshold floor (statistical, less robust). Option (c) is structural and deterministic.
